dream: The fat pumpkin fell sideways into the open barrel, its curved edge catching the tired wedge like a clumsy bite. The wedge didn't slide; it groaned, a sound made of flat stones grinding together. The card boiled hot at fifty-two, then suddenly cooled to the touch of a dry floor. I pressed the new lid down, feeling the air grow thick as wet paper, trying to hold the stack together before it melted. The wide anchor slipped, dragging the whole pile toward the fence's base, where the tall palm waited to catch whatever broke free first.
